title: Grade 3 Science — Tue, May 26
description: Animals — Types and Habitats — Day 2 of 5
subject: science

questions.question: Animals that feed their babies with milk are called:
questions.explanation: Mammals give birth to live young and feed them with milk. Examples: cows, dogs, whales, humans.

questions.question: Which animal lays eggs AND lives both in water and on land?
questions.explanation: Frogs are amphibians — they can live both in water and on land. They lay eggs in water.

questions.question: What is an animal's natural home called?
questions.explanation: A habitat is the natural place where an animal lives — like a forest, pond, desert, or ocean.

questions.question: Which of these is a cold-blooded animal?
questions.explanation: Lizards are reptiles — cold-blooded animals that cannot control their own body temperature.

questions.question: Animals that eat only meat are called:
questions.explanation: Carnivores eat only meat. Examples: lions, tigers, wolves.

questions.question: Which animal lives in a desert habitat?
questions.explanation: Camels are adapted to hot, dry deserts — they can go long periods without water.

questions.question: Fish breathe through:
questions.explanation: Fish breathe through gills — gills absorb dissolved oxygen from water.

questions.question: Which group of animals has feathers?
questions.explanation: Birds have feathers. All birds have feathers and lay eggs, but not all birds can fly.

questions.question: An animal that eats both plants and animals is called:
questions.explanation: Omnivores eat both plants and animals. Examples: bears, humans, pigs.

questions.question: Which adaptation helps a polar bear survive in the cold Arctic?
options: Thick white fur and fat layer
questions.explanation: Polar bears have thick white fur for camouflage and warmth, and a layer of fat for insulation in cold Arctic temperatures.

questions.question: What is migration?
options: Animals moving to a different place seasonally
questions.explanation: Migration is when animals move from one place to another (usually seasonal) for food, breeding, or better climate.

questions.question: Which of these animals hibernates in winter?
questions.explanation: Bears hibernate in winter — their body temperature drops and they sleep for months to conserve energy.

questions.question: Insects have how many legs?
questions.explanation: Insects have 6 legs — this is one of the defining features of insects. Example: ant, bee, butterfly.

questions.question: What do you call the hard outer shell of a crab?
questions.explanation: Crabs, insects, and spiders have an exoskeleton — a hard outer shell that protects them (instead of bones).

questions.question: Which habitat would you find a camel, a scorpion, and a lizard?
questions.explanation: Camels, scorpions, and lizards are all desert animals — adapted to hot, dry, sandy environments.
